title: head-stride prefetch and quantization-hinting for model-specific attention unrolling (LLama/Mistral/Qwen)
author: Nina Patel
description: Motivation: observed p95 latency regressions on real workloads for some model variants (LLama MQA splits, Mistral gated heads, Qwen block-aligned attention) under continuous batching. Root cause analysis showed misaligned per-head memory accesses and non-optimal kernel selection when head counts or per-head dims diverge from kernel tiling assumptions. This PR introduces a head-stride prefetcher and a lightweight per-layer quantization-hinting API to guide kernel selection and attention unrolling. Goals: (1) reduce head-wise memory stall cycles caused by scattered KV lookups, (2) enable model-specific kernel hints so the runtime picks vectorized attention paths for common MQA/GQA layouts, (3) preserve correctness and provide automatic fallbacks for unsupported head shapes. Summary of changes: added a HeadStridePrefetcher in runtime/kv that computes an access schedule for KV slabs based on observed head_stride and token_alignment; the prefetcher issues asynchronous GPU prefetches when batch composition and sequence-length distribution indicate benefit; added ModelQuantHints struct and a small registry in runtime/model_hints.cpp allowing onboarding to register recommended kernel variants (e.g., head-wise pad sizes, preferred unroll factor, quant tile width); extended kernel_router to consult ModelQuantHints before scoring candidate kernels and to add a small runtime penalty for fallback kernels; updated continuous-batcher to tag requests with head_stride metadata and to allow batching windows to prefer alignment-aware coalescing; implemented a compatibility shim that detects MQA/GQA layouts (variable heads per layer) and maps them to nearest supported kernel with transparent permute paths. Implementation notes: prefetcher is best-effort and can be disabled via env REDWOOD_HEAD_PREFETCH=0; quant-hints are opt-in per-model and do not change serialized weights; kernel_router scoring uses a new cost heuristic (memory_stride_cost + compute_efficiency_score + hint_bonus). Benchmarks: internal perf-lab microbenchmarks on rtx-a40 and gpus in perf-canary show p95 latency improvements of 6-12% on Llama-3-13B MQA workloads, 4-9% throughput increase on Mistral-medium gated-head scenarios, and 3-7% p95 reduction on Qwen-14B with block-aligned attention sequences; end-to-end customer-like traces (chat-like short seqs) showed median latency circa 5% improvement with no increase in token error rates. Rollout plan: feature gated behind model_hints registry; enable default prefetch for models registered in this PR after one week of perf-canary stability; rollback knob via feature flag. Testing: unit tests for ModelQuantHints, property tests for kernel selection fallbacks, GPU integration tests for prefetch retirements, and perf CI profiles added. Related: links to ENG-4821 and ENG-4900 for scheduling follow-ups. See release_notes for user-visible impact and config knobs.

release_notes: Improves latency and throughput for certain Llama/Mistral/Qwen layouts by introducing head-stride prefetching and model quantization hints. Feature is opt-in via model_hints registry; ops can disable prefetch with REDWOOD_HEAD_PREFETCH=0.
